datapoints.unit: active app-based workers (rideshare + delivery, Flex member platforms)
datapoints.source: Flex Association / Public First, 'App-Based Industry Impact: California' one-pager
datapoints.verbatim: 870,000 active app-based workers in California ... $38B economic impact for California ... 660M app-based platform transactions in California ... Sources: Economic impact data from Public First analysis of Flex member rideshare and delivery data for 2022. Survey data from Morning Consult 2023 survey.
datapoints.notes: Industry trade group (DoorDash, Grubhub, HopSkipDrive, Instacart, Lyft, Shipt, Uber). 'Active' is not defined on the CA one-pager or on the national microsite; national report says figures come from 'aggregated internal data from major app-based rideshare and delivery platforms' and workers use 'an average of 1.9 platforms', so it is unclear whether 870k is deduplicated across platforms. No rideshare/delivery split given. No 2025-2026 California update located (searched flexassociation.org and flex.publicfirst.co).

datapoints.unit: active drivers and delivery partners
datapoints.source: Flex Association / Public First national economic impact report
datapoints.verbatim: 7.3 million active drivers and delivery partners ... 4.3 billion rides and deliveries ... an average of 1.9 platforms
datapoints.notes: Context for the CA figure: CA = 870k/7.3M = 11.9% of national active workers on the same basis. US one-pager also cites $212B contribution, 2.1M jobs supported, 4.3B transactions.

datapoints.unit: unique driver registrations completing >=1 ride or delivery (DoorDash+Instacart+Lyft+Uber), Q4 2020-Q3 2021
datapoints.source: UC Riverside School of Business Center for Economic Forecasting and Development, 'An Analysis of App-Based Drivers in California' (commissioned by Protect App-Based Drivers + Services)
datapoints.verbatim: From fourth-quarter 2020 to third-quarter 2021, there were around 1.37 million drivers who performed at least one ride or delivery across the DoorDash, Instacart, Lyft, and Uber platforms in California. Drivers are registered across multiple apps, but the extent to which this occurs is not fully known.
datapoints.notes: Definition (report appendix): 'The registration count of unique app-based drivers who completed at least one ride/delivery in California in the periods of study. This may include duplicate drivers across platforms.' Industry-funded but based on direct platform data with independent UCR access. Likely the origin of the USC/NEA '1.3 million Californians' figure.

datapoints.unit: driver registrations completing >=1 ride or delivery in the quarter (4 platforms)
datapoints.source: UC Riverside CEFD, 'An Analysis of App-Based Drivers in California'
datapoints.verbatim: In third-quarter 2021, 800,000 drivers completed one ride or delivery on the platforms. This represents a 41% increase compared to the number of drivers registered across the platforms in third-quarter 2020. ... In third-quarter 2021, there were nearly 140 million trips and deliveries in California across the platforms in the state. [chart value: 138.7 million]
datapoints.notes: Quarterly-active count is the closest thing to a 'currently active' denominator; 138.7M trips+deliveries per quarter / 800k drivers = ~173 per active driver per quarter. Not split rideshare vs delivery. LA-Long Beach-Anaheim appears only in the hourly-earnings table (no LA driver count).

datapoints.value: two-thirds of drivers <5 engaged hrs/week on any one platform; survey: 36% <14 hrs/wk, 22% 15-20, 18% 21-30, 22% >30
datapoints.unit: share of drivers
datapoints.source: UC Riverside CEFD (platform data + EMC Research driver survey, invitations to 625,000 drivers)
datapoints.verbatim: As of third-quarter 2021, two-thirds of drivers worked with any one platform for fewer than five hours per week. ... 36% of respondents report driving on platforms for fewer than 14 hours per week; another 22% of respondents report driving on platforms for 15 to 20 hours per week; 18% report driving on platforms for 21 to 30 hours per week; and 22% report driving on platforms for more than 30 hours per week. Additionally, only 23% of drivers report working with platforms on what would conventionally be considered a full-time basis. Seventy-seven percent of respondents report working with platforms on a part-time basis (45%) or only occasionally (32%).
datapoints.notes: Useful for converting quarterly/annual-active counts to daily-active. Survey sample skews to engaged drivers (active in prior 3 months). 'An email invitation was sent to 625,000 drivers across Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, and Instacart' - i.e., ~625k CA drivers active in the 3 months before Sept 2021.

datapoints.unit: Californians who drove for rideshare and food delivery companies
datapoints.source: USC Equity Research Institute / National Equity Atlas, 'Prop 22 Depresses Wages and Deepens Inequities for California Workers'
datapoints.verbatim: From 2020 to 2021, 1.3 million Californians drove for rideshare and food delivery companies.
datapoints.notes: Almost certainly restates the UCR CEFD 1.37M platform-registration figure (which double-counts multi-app workers). Study itself surveyed only 55 rideshare drivers; no delivery/rideshare split, no LA figure.

datapoints.unit: rideshare (TNC) drivers covered by AB 1340
datapoints.source: Office of Sen. Dave Cortese, AB 1340 (Transportation Network Company Drivers Labor Relations Act) press release
datapoints.verbatim: establishes collective bargaining rights for more than 800,000 rideshare drivers
datapoints.notes: Legislative/advocacy talking point; no methodology. AB 1340 covers TNC (Uber/Lyft) drivers only, not delivery couriers. Caution: the same '800,000' number appears in the UCR CEFD report as the Q3-2021 count of ALL four-platform (ride + delivery) registrations, so this may be a conflation rather than a rideshare-only count. Also reported by CalMatters/Stocktonia (Jul 2025) as 'more than 800,000'.

datapoints.unit: gig workers in the state (Prop 22-covered)
datapoints.source: KQED
datapoints.verbatim: a case that could change the fate of more than 1 million gig workers in the state
datapoints.notes: Unattributed round number; CBS SF used the same '1M gig workers' framing for the Prop 22 Supreme Court case. Consistent with Flex 870k / UCR 800k-1.37M.

datapoints.unit: share of California workforce engaging in app-based work
datapoints.source: Axios San Diego citing Flex Association study
datapoints.verbatim: about 5% of California's overall workforce engages in app-based work like DoorDash, Uber or Lyft ... 870,000 workers in the app-based rideshare and delivery industry in 2022
datapoints.notes: Secondary citation of the Flex figure (870k / ~18M CA labor force ~ 4.8%).

datapoints.unit: app-based delivery (non-rideshare) workers
datapoints.source: none located
datapoints.notes: GAP: no study or disclosure giving a California delivery-only headcount was found. All CA counts (Flex 870k 2022; UCR 1.37M 4Q-2020-21 / 800k Q3-2021; USC 1.3M; AB1340 800k rideshare) are either combined ride+delivery or rideshare-only. Closest delivery-specific CA data: DoorDash says California Dashers averaged 'roughly six hours per week on delivery' in Q4 2023 (about.doordash.com Prop 22 post, May 17, 2024) and only DoorDash has a data-sharing agreement with Covered California. UC Berkeley Labor Center five-metro study (May 20, 2024; 1,088 drivers, 52,370 trips, Jan 2022, incl. Los Angeles) gives delivery pay, not headcounts. Travel Behaviour & Society 2026 (Shaheen/Wolfe/Cohen, vol 44, 101218) is a literature review (n=41), expert interviews (n=8), case studies (n=7), Oct 2022-May 2024 - no headcount or share.

datapoints.unit: share of eligible DoorDash Dashers using the Prop 22 healthcare stipend
datapoints.source: DoorDash, 'Thanks to California's Prop 22 Dashers are Doing Better than Ever'
datapoints.verbatim: Only 11% of eligible Dashers used the healthcare stipend ... 80% of Dashers reported having coverage through other sources ... California Dashers averaged roughly six hours per week on delivery [Q4 2023]
datapoints.notes: Share only; DoorDash does not publish the absolute number of eligible (>=15 engaged hrs/wk) or enrolled Dashers. National Equity Atlas survey (nationalequityatlas.org/research/analyses/rideshare-drivers-healthcare-prop-22; page returned HTTP 403) independently found 'Only 11 percent of study participants reported receiving a stipend' (2023 survey of CA rideshare drivers, per search snippet). No state (Covered California / CalHHS) enrollment counts found; a broker FAQ notes 'Covered California only has a data sharing agreement with DoorDash'. 2026 full stipend is $579/month (coverhealthca.com). GAP: absolute enrollment counts by year.

datapoints.unit: Dashers in California
datapoints.source: DoorDash / Public First 2024 and 2025 US impact reports; DoorDash Prop 22 post
datapoints.verbatim: [2025 report] More than 8 million people dashed in the U.S. in 2025 ... approximately 4 hours per week in Q4 2025 ... the typical Dasher was active for about 10 weeks in total ... earning nearly $20 billion, including tips. [2024 report, doordash2024.publicfirst.co] 7 million Dashers earned through DoorDash in 2024; an active Dasher is one who 'delivered an order through the DoorDash platform in 2024'. [Prop 22 post, May 2024] California Dashers earned around $36 per hour while on deliveries in 2023 ... Los Angeles: around $35/hour ... averaged roughly six hours per week on delivery [Q4 2023].
datapoints.notes: GAP: neither the 2024 nor 2025 Public First microsite has state-level Dasher counts or state pages; no 'X Dashers in California/Los Angeles' statement found. DoorDash merchants page says 'Greater Los Angeles has the highest volume of orders' among its markets (merchants.doordash.com/en-us/locations-los-angeles, undated). Third-party stat sites cite '2 million monthly active Dashers' (US) - unverified. The 8M-annual / ~4 hrs-per-week / ~10-weeks-active figures are the best published inputs for an annual-active -> daily-active conversion.

datapoints.unit: Uber drivers in California (rideshare; couriers not stated)
datapoints.year: 2020 (Uber economist Alison Stein); recycled by third-party sites as 'late 2025'
datapoints.source: The Rideshare Guy / notta.ai citing Uber economist Alison Stein (2020 reclassification analysis)
datapoints.verbatim: In 2020, Uber economist Alison Stein reported that California had 209,000 Uber drivers. [notta.ai: 'As of late 2025 ... California accounts for approximately 209,000 active Uber drivers out of roughly 1 million active Uber drivers in the United States']
datapoints.notes: GAP: no official Uber 'in California' or 'in Los Angeles' driver/courier fact page found; uber.publicfirst.co does not resolve. Uber newsroom (Apr 25, 2024, 'Uber invests more than $1 billion in Prop 22 benefits for CA Drivers and Couriers') gives no headcount; it reports median $33/utilized hour (Q4 2023), stipend up to $489.54/month, ~90% driver support. The 209k figure is 2020 and rideshare-only; the 'late 2025' framing on notta.ai appears to be the same number recycled. Uber global: ~10M active drivers and couriers (2025, Wikipedia/Uber).

datapoints.unit: gig/freelance workers in Los Angeles (broad definition, not app-based)
datapoints.year: 2018 data (study released 2019; Instawork post Apr 4, 2019, updated Mar 18, 2026)
datapoints.source: Instawork blog citing Fiverr-commissioned Rockbridge Associates study
datapoints.verbatim: about 400,000 workers who collectively earned more than $18 billion last year
datapoints.notes: GAP: the primary source for a '450,000 gig workers in LA County' figure was NOT found; no UCLA Labor Center, LAEDC, or LA County/City document with that number surfaced. UCLA Labor Center's 'More Than a Gig' (2018) is a survey of ~260 LA ride-hail drivers with no headcount. The 400k Fiverr/Rockbridge figure covers all freelancers/independent workers (design, writing, etc.), so it is not an app-based courier count. Search also surfaced 'in Los Angeles, 71 percent of [gig] workers are full time' (same Fiverr study family).

datapoints.unit: nonemployer establishments, NAICS 492 Couriers and Messengers
datapoints.source: U.S. Census Bureau Nonemployer Statistics 2023, county file nonemp23co
datapoints.verbatim: ST=06, CTY=037, NAICS=492, ESTAB=44977, RCPTOT=866628 (thousands of dollars)
datapoints.notes: 2022 value: 44,076 establishments, $799,739K receipts (nonemp22co.zip). All-industry LA County nonemployers 2023: 1,128,124. NAICS 492 nonemployers = self-employed couriers filing a Schedule C/1099 with >= $1,000 receipts; includes app food couriers, Amazon Flex, parcel/messenger sole proprietors; app rideshare drivers generally code to NAICS 485 (taxi/limo), so 492 is a delivery-leaning proxy. Undercounts workers who never file or code elsewhere. api.census.gov now requires an API key (returned 'Missing Key'), so bulk files were used.

datapoints.unit: nonemployer establishments, NAICS 492
datapoints.source: U.S. Census Bureau Nonemployer Statistics 2023, county file
datapoints.verbatim: ST=06, CTY=075, NAICS=492, ESTAB=3187, RCPTOT=69516 (thousands of dollars)
datapoints.notes: 2022 value: 3,615 establishments, $71,385K receipts. SF County all-industry nonemployers 2023: 87,009. LA:SF ratio for NAICS 492 = 14.1x (2023).

datapoints.unit: nonemployer establishments, NAICS 492
datapoints.source: U.S. Census Bureau Nonemployer Statistics 2023, state file nonemp23st
datapoints.verbatim: ST=06, NAICS=492, LFO=- (all), ESTAB=171603, RCPTOT=3042798 (thousands of dollars); LFO=S (sole proprietorships) ESTAB=170956
datapoints.notes: 2022 value: 175,111 (sole props 174,520), $2,764,320K receipts. LA County share of CA NAICS 492 nonemployers: 44,977/171,603 = 26.2% (2023); 44,076/175,111 = 25.2% (2022). Average receipts per CA 492 nonemployer 2023 = ~$17.7K, consistent with part-time gig delivery.

datapoints.unit: LA County population / California population
datapoints.source: California Department of Finance, E-1 Population Estimates press release, May 1, 2026
datapoints.verbatim: The 0.14-percent decline to 39,593,000 marks the first year of population loss after three consecutive years of population increases ... California's 58 counties range in size from Alpine County, with just over 1,180 residents, to Los Angeles County with 9.8 million residents. [table: Los Angeles 9,900,914 (1/1/2025) -> 9,837,286 (1/1/2026); California 39,646,907 (1/1/2025) -> 39,592,978 (1/1/2026)]

datapoints.unit: LA County / California private employment, NAICS 722 Food Services and Drinking Places
datapoints.source: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, industry 722 file, 2025 Q2
datapoints.verbatim: area_fips 06037 own_code 5 industry 722 2025 Q2: qtrly_estabs 23,099; month3_emplvl 386,521; avg_wkly_wage $680. area_fips 06000 own_code 5: qtrly_estabs 87,929; month3_emplvl 1,454,354; avg_wkly_wage $655. area_fips 06075 own_code 5: qtrly_estabs 3,773; month3_emplvl 55,208.
datapoints.notes: 386,521 / 1,454,354 = 26.58% (June 2025). Q1 2025 (March): LA 382,137 / CA 1,426,579 = 26.79% (https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2025/1/industry/722.csv). Establishment share: 23,099/87,929 = 26.3%. SF County = 3.8% of CA. LA's restaurant-employment share (~26.6%) exceeds its population share (~24.9%), consistent with LA over-indexing on delivery demand.

datapoints.unit: app-based food-delivery couriers in Los Angeles
datapoints.source: none located
datapoints.notes: GAP: no press, platform, academic, or government estimate of the number of app-based delivery couriers in LA was found. Searches for 'delivery drivers in Los Angeles' estimates returned only salary/job pages. DoorDash states Greater LA is its highest-order-volume market but gives no Dasher count; DoorDash LA Dashers earned ~$35/hr on-delivery in 2023. UCR CEFD 2022 gives Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim hourly earnings only. UCLA Labor Center LA work covers ride-hail (2018) and undocumented drivers (LA Public Press, May 2025), not courier counts.

datapoints.value: not yet published (2017: 1.0% of employment electronically mediated)
datapoints.unit: share of total employment
datapoints.source: BLS Contingent and Alternative Employment Arrangements FAQ (July 2023 CWS)
datapoints.verbatim: Questions to identify digital labor platform employment (app-based work) were added, replacing the previous items on electronically mediated employment from 2017. ... BLS intends to publish additional estimates from this supplement in the future. [2017 recode: electronically mediated workers accounted for 1.0 percent of total employment in May 2017]
datapoints.notes: As of the FAQ/Nov 8 2024 release, the 2023 digital-platform-employment estimates had not been published; verify whether BLS released them in 2025-2026 before using. 1.0% of ~153M employed (2017) ~ 1.6M; a CA/LA cut would need microdata.

datapoints.unit: drivers in sample (52,370 trips), five metros incl. Los Angeles
datapoints.geography: Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, SF Bay, Seattle
datapoints.source: UC Berkeley Labor Center, 'Gig Passenger and Delivery Driver Pay in Five Metro Areas'
datapoints.verbatim: 52,370 trips ... 1,088 drivers ... January 2022 in the Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, San Francisco Bay, and Seattle metros
datapoints.notes: Pay study only; no headcounts and no delivery/rideshare worker split published on the landing page. Earlier Berkeley/NEA CA study (May 2024) found delivery workers net $5.93/hr after expenses before tips.

gaps: No 2025-2026 update to the Flex/Public First California count (870,000 is 2022 data); Flex does not define 'active' or state whether the count is deduplicated across platforms (workers average 1.9 platforms), and gives no rideshare/delivery split.
No California delivery-only (non-rideshare) headcount from any study, platform, or state agency; Berkeley Labor Center / USC / NEA / UC ITS work reports pay, not counts.

Prop 22 healthcare-stipend data are shares only (DoorDash: 11% of eligible Dashers, Q4 2023; NEA survey: 11% of participants); no absolute enrollment counts by year from Covered California, CalHHS, or platforms. nationalequityatlas.org returned HTTP 403.
No DoorDash 'Dashers in California / Los Angeles' count: the 2024 and 2025 Public First microsites are national-only with no state pages.

No official Uber 'in California' / 'in Los Angeles' driver-and-courier count; only a 2020 rideshare figure (209,000) recycled by third-party sites. uber.publicfirst.co does not exist. Grubhub/Instacart CA counts not found.

Primary source for '450,000 gig workers in LA County' not found; no UCLA Labor Center, LAEDC, LA City, or LA County document with an app-based courier estimate for 2023-2026 surfaced. Closest is a 2018-19 Fiverr/Rockbridge '400,000 gig workers in Los Angeles' (all freelancers).
No direct press or research estimate of LA-area food-delivery couriers.
BLS 2023 CWS digital-platform-employment estimates: publication status after Nov 2024 not verified.
IRS 1099-K/NEC gig data with an LA breakdown not searched (budget); AB 1340 official Senate/Assembly committee analyses not fetched (only the Cortese press release with '800,000 rideshare drivers').
Census NES 2024 (would be released ~mid-2026) not checked; api.census.gov now requires a key so bulk historical-datasets files were used for 2022 and 2023.
